LLM auditresponse for obsidian-bin.install:
<security_assessment>
  <decision>SAFE</decision>
  <details>
    The file is a Bash script named `obsidian-bin.install` intended for installing Obsidian from the AUR. It defines a `note` function and two post‑install functions called `post_install` and `post_remove`. Variables `all_off`, `bold`, `blue`, `yellow` are created with `tput` commands. The script first checks whether `/proc/self/ns/user` is a symbolic link and whether `unshare --user true` succeeds; if so it applies mode `4755` to `/opt/Obsidian/chrome-sandbox`, otherwise `0755`. It then runs `hash update-mime-database` and `hash update-desktop-database`; if the hashes succeed it invokes the corresponding update tools. Finally it copies an AppArmor profile from `/opt/Obsidian/resources/apparmor-profile` to `/etc/apparmor.d/obsidian` using `apparmor_parser`.

    There are no network calls, no `curl`, `wget`, or `eval`. All actions are local file operations (chmod, cp, update commands). The use of `unshare --user` and `hash` is uncommon but not inherently malicious; they perform privilege isolation and integrity checks. The script does not attempt to reach external hosts, exfiltrate data, or execute injected code. It follows standard AUR packaging patterns such as post‑install hooks and AppArmor profile handling. Hence no evidence of a supply‑chain attack.
  </details>
  <evidence></evidence>
  <summary>Script performs safe post-install tasks, no external downloads.</summary>
</security_assessment>
